YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Rules this tool checks for you (it returns an "Error: ..." message instead of booking when one is broken):
- Every payment_id must be an id that appears in the user's profile "payment_methods"
(call get_user_details). NEVER invent an id from a card's last four digits.
- At most ONE certificate, at most ONE credit card and at most THREE gift cards per reservation.
- A certificate or gift card amount cannot be larger than its balance.
- The amounts must add up exactly to the total price
(sum of flight prices x passengers + $30 x passengers if insurance + $50 x nonfree_baggages).
- A passenger whose name is the account holder (or a saved passenger in the profile) is booked
with the date of birth stored in the profile. Do not make up a date of birth.

one reservation per passenger so each one can use its own certificate), that is allowed. Call this
tool once per reservation, each with its own passengers and its own payment_methods.

plus $5 on one credit card, no bags, no insurance). Ids in <...> must be copied from get_user_details:

def calculate_flight_change_cost(reservation_id: str, cabin: str, flights: list):
Compute the EXACT amount the user will be charged (or refunded) by update_reservation_flights,
WITHOUT changing anything. Call this BEFORE you tell the user the price of a flight change or a
cabin change (upgrade), and quote the "user_will_pay" value it returns. Do not compute the price yourself.
How the price works (the tool applies this for you):
- The cabin applies to EVERY flight of the reservation. When the cabin changes, ALL flights,
including the return flights you are not changing, are re-priced at the new cabin's current price.
- A flight is kept at its old price only if the flight number, date AND cabin are all unchanged.
- Charge = (sum of new prices x passengers) - (sum of old prices x passengers). A negative value is a refund.
Example: upgrade reservation 'ABC123' (2 flights, cabin economy) to business without changing flights:

flights: The ENTIRE new list of flights (same list you will pass to update_reservation_flights), each {"flight_number": "HAT001", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}, including unchanged flights.
A dict with per-flight old/new prices, passenger count, old_total, new_total and user_will_pay
(positive = the user pays this amount, negative = refund), or an "Error: ..." string.

Before calling: get the user id, the reservation id, the reason for cancellation, and an explicit
This tool checks the cancellation policy in code and returns "Error: ..." WITHOUT cancelling when the
reservation is not eligible. A reservation is eligible only if NO flight has been flown yet AND at
least one of these is true:
1. it was booked within the last 24 hours (created_at at or after 2024-05-14 15:00:00), or
2. a flight in it was cancelled by the airline, or
4. it has travel insurance AND the user's reason is a covered reason (health or weather).
Travel insurance does NOT cover "change of plan" or other reasons: if the user's reason is a change
of plan and rules 1-3 do not apply, do NOT call this tool; tell the user it cannot be cancelled.
Membership level (silver, gold, ...) does NOT make a reservation eligible.
If the tool refuses, tell the user the reservation cannot be cancelled and why. Do not transfer to a
human agent just because cancellation is refused (only transfer if the user explicitly asks).
